components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Switch
components.description: RUN AT LOGIN in the header and SHOW ON THE LIGHT BAR on SETTINGS: a fixed label and a square switch. On is a red track with the knob at the right; off a grey edged track with the knob at the left. While a change runs, the knob shows the side asked for in Disabled grey and the switch takes no clicks.

narrative.overview:
The window is one keyboard set as a bitmap type specimen on black. Headings, tabs, labels, numbers and key legends all come from one pixel face, Silkscreen, pre-rasterized into cells and painted as flat rectangles. Every cell and every shape lands on whole device pixels, so the lettering echoes the keyboard's own dot screen and stays sharp at 100, 125, 150 and 200 percent display scale. Archivo carries only running prose and numeric readouts.

The density is that of a working instrument: three fixed columns under a 64pt header, ruled boxes, no ornament beyond the dot-matrix patch. Colour belongs to the keyboard. LED colours appear as flat fills of the exact RGB sent, while the chrome stays in near-black greys with three signal colours that each mean one thing. The interface is dark by commitment.

Rejected outright: the RGB-suite default of a charcoal window with a product render, a colour wheel and glow. Also rejected, by the user's standing rules: cream or off-white grounds, italic accent words, numbered section labels, monospace labels and pill buttons.
keyCharacteristics: Bitmap caps for every heading, tab, label, number and key legend; Archivo for prose and readouts only.
Whole-device-pixel geometry everywhere, with antialiasing (feathering) off.
Square corners on every surface, control and key.
LED colours as flat exact-RGB fills, never glowed, shaded or gradiented.
Red, green and amber each reserved for one meaning.
The dot-matrix patch as the single house texture.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Red means selected, active, focused or primary; green means connected or observed; amber means warning or differing proof. No signal colour decorates, and no other hue enters the chrome.

rules.name: The Keyboard Owns Colour Rule
rules.body: Any hue outside the signals on screen is an LED colour the user chose, shown as a flat fill of its exact RGB. A user colour that happens to be red or green is still content, not a signal.

rules.name: The Quiet Disabled Rule
rules.body: A disabled control is Disabled-grey text with no edge and no fill, so it reads as absent rather than as a faint button.

rules.name: The Whole Cell Rule
rules.body: A bitmap cell is its point size times the display scale, rounded to whole device pixels with a +0.01 bias (so 1.4999 rounds like 1.5), and never smaller than one device pixel. Bitmap text is never scaled, smoothed or drawn as an outline font.

rules.name: The No Monospace Rule
rules.body: egui's monospace family is mapped to Archivo. Labels are bitmap caps or Archivo, never a monospace face.

rules.name: The Whole Legend Rule
rules.body: A key shows its full label if it fits in the key's width minus 8pt, else the definition's `short` legend, else nothing. Words are never cut.

rules.name: The Snapped Geometry Rule
rules.body: Every rectangle passes through `snap()` and every line width through `line()`: edges and widths land on whole device pixels, lines at least one pixel wide. Feathering is off globally, so a non-snapped shape shows as a visible jag. Keep it that way.

rules.name: The Flat Light Rule
rules.body: An LED colour is a flat fill of the exact RGB, with no glow, bloom, gradient or shading. The picker's saturation and value field (24 x 24 cells) and hue strip (48 cells) are built from flat snapped cells, not smooth gradients.

dos: Do draw every bitmap word with `px_text` at one of the seven sizes (cells of 1, 1.5, 2, 4 or 6pt) and snap every shape with `snap()`, `line()`, `fill()` and `outline()`.
Do keep feathering off and keep the +0.01 rounding bias in `whole()`.
Do show LED colour as a flat fill of the exact RGB the keyboard receives.

Do reserve Signal Red for selection, the active tab, focus, the switches when on and each context's primary action; Observed Green for connected and observed; Caution Amber for warnings and differing proof.
Do render disabled controls as Disabled-grey text with no edge.
Do keep proof states distinct: observed, differs, and unmarked layout data.
Do fall back from full label to `short` legend to no legend on keys.
donts: Don't add glow, gradients, shadows or rounded corners to keys, swatches or controls.
Don't use red, green or amber for decoration or for a meaning other than its own.
Don't set bitmap text in mixed case, at a non-whole cell size, or through a vector font.
Don't use cream or off-white grounds, italic accent words, numbered section labels, monospace labels or pill buttons.
Don't add a product render, colour wheel or charcoal RGB-suite chrome.
